generation.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Electric Power Monthly (Form EIA-923), net generation by state and source, grouped by the ERW (docs/methods/generation_mix.md)
generation.hourly_reason: No public source gives a state's generation by the hour; the hourly picture is by balancing authority, in the Grid tool.

retail.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-861M, retail sales and average price by state and sector
retail.revenue_note: Revenue is EIA's sales times EIA's average price for the same month and sector. EIA computes its average price as revenue over sales, so the product gives EIA's revenue to within the price's rounding (one tenth of a dollar a MWh).

plants.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Preliminary Monthly Electric Generator Inventory (Form EIA-860M)
plants.unit: MW (nameplate and net summer); MWh (storage energy)
plants.retired_note: EIA-860M's retired sheet as the ERW's table holds it: the generators retired in its window, not every retirement since 2001.

co2.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles, emissions by state by fuel
co2.unit: metric tons of CO2; kg of CO2 per MWh

gas.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Natural Gas Monthly, consumption by end use and production by state
gas.production_reason: EIA prints no marketed production for New Jersey: it is not a producing state in the Natural Gas Monthly

energy.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Energy Data System

by_sector_reason.commercial: the warehouse's SEDS tables hold the commercial sector's electricity and natural gas, not its total energy
by_sector_reason.transportation: the warehouse's SEDS tables hold the transportation sector's electricity and natural gas, not its total energy

disposition.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, State Electricity Profiles, source and disposition
disposition.note: Net interstate trade is EIA's figure, a line of the disposition: positive where the state sent more electricity to other states than it took in from them, below zero where it took in more.

serving.source: U.S. Census Bureau county population estimates, and Form EIA-861's utilities and balancing authorities by county, as the ERW's table eia_county_region joins them
serving.basis: Each county counts once, whole, for its primary authority: the one whose utilities serve most of the county's customers in EIA-861. A county two authorities share is counted for its primary one.

large_load_laws.source: The ERW's large-load research files, each law read at its legislature's or regulator's own page

laws.bill: A. 796 (Fourth Reprint), P.L. 2026, c.32 (Data Center Fair Share Act)
laws.title: An Act concerning the provision of electricity to certain data centers and supplementing Title 48 of the Revised Statutes.
laws.threshold: set by the BPU for each utility at not greater than 50 MW, with related data centers aggregated
laws.requirements: commission rulemaking: the BPU must set standards by order for every electric public utility within 12 months; each utility must then petition for a large data center rate class and tariff [p. 1, Section 1b: "No later than 12 months after the effective date of this section, the Board of Public Utilities shall establish, by order for every electric public utility, standards for the provision of electricity to large data center customers by electric public utilities." | p. 1, Section 1c: "each electric public utility shall file a petition with the board for approval of a rate class and tariff for the provision of electricity to large data center customers."] || minimum bill: adequate financial guarantees to pay for at least 85 percent of the electricity supply requested, for 10 years from when service commences, unless the BPU's standards say otherwise [p. 1, Section 1d(1): "data center customer provides adequate financial guarantees that it will pay for at least 85 percent of the ... it requests for a period of 10 years from when service commences or as otherwise determined in the board"] || collateral: deposits, financial security or, for customers with sufficiently high credit ratings, financial commitments, in forms the BPU approves, over the 10-year period [p. 1, Section 1d(2): "provide for the posting of deposits, financial security, or, for ... center customers with sufficiently high credit ratings, financial commitments, in respective forms approved by the board"] || exit fee: no exit fee printed; the BPU may approve a stranded cost recovery mechanism applicable only to the large data center class [p. 1, Section 1d(2): "authorize the board to approve a stranded cost recovery mechanism applicable exclusively to the large data center customer class"] || interconnection study: new large data center customers pay the reasonable costs of interconnection, system impact and facilities studies [p. 1, Section 1d(8): "require any new large data center customer to ... pay the reasonable costs of any interconnection, system impact, and facilities"] || curtailment or backup generation: priority curtailment of large data center customers before residential customers in system emergencies, as firm load shed; demand flexibility commitments [p. 1, Section 1b(11): "ensure the priority curtailment of large data ... center customers before residential customers, excluding designated critical" | p. 1, Section 1d(5): "(5) require demand flexibility commitments by large"]

severance.reason: the severance tool holds Texas, Louisiana, New Mexico only
